summary: LA County Forestry enclosed timber lookout on Parker Mountain, built 1935, staffed 1938 and 1949, closed 1969; tower demolished, concrete base remains.

facts.design: Enclosed timber tower on a 14 by 14 ft wood cab built to a 1934 USFS Region 5 standard
facts.status_note: Listed as demolished by Angeles Adventures; a concrete structure remains at the top

access.note: Angeles Adventures calls most of the mountain BLM-managed public land; the roads around its base are private and parking is hard

visit.trail_note: Mainly fire road to the top, per Angeles Adventures

events.note: Angeles Adventures and the 1935 Forest Lookouts entry date it to 1935; a November 1934 item says construction was under way
Theo L. Mercy named as lookout staff
Cecil G. Harrell named as lookout staff
Closed down July 22, 1969; helicopter detection made the tower obsolete

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Angeles Adventures places the mountain in Acton; the Forest Lookouts 1969 entry says the lookout was east of Saugus. The story uses Acton, the location Angeles Adventures gives for the mountain.
A November 1934 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts says construction was under way; Forest Lookouts and Angeles Adventures date the completed lookout to 1935. The story says built 1935.
Angeles Adventures gives 4131 ft in its header and 4,144 feet in its text. No elevation is used in the story or the facts.

notes_for_editor: Ownership is 'unknown' in the record; no source read names the owner of the tower site, and Angeles Adventures calls most of the mountain BLM public land. The access level 'public' rests on that land-status line; the roads at the base are private, and no rule on entry to the old site was found. The Sage Menu page is a user-review hiking listing and is used only to corroborate the concrete base that Angeles Adventures also describes. Record kind 'enclosed_tower', status 'gone', coordinates and agency match the sources. Two searches turned up no demolition date and no staff beyond 1938 and 1949.
